subject.title: fix embedded compaction hook reset API

question: Should OpenClaw permanently expose a current-session reset capability to successful after-compaction plugin hooks, and if so should the contract be limited to `resetSession(reason?)`?
rationale: This creates a new plugin authority over persisted session lifecycle and defines which compaction implementations expose it; repository policy requires an owner decision rather than inferring a permanent API from a plugin-specific workaround.

options.title: Approve the narrow hook contract
options.body: Keep only `resetSession(reason?)` on successful, unlocked after-compaction contexts with lifecycle-owned draining, documentation, focused compatibility tests, and complete live proof.

options.title: Broaden session lifecycle APIs
options.body: Pause this branch and design reset, compaction, and lifecycle control as one explicit plugin SDK contract with migration and ownership guidance.

options.title: Keep reset policy outside core
options.body: Decline the new hook API and require memory plugins to use an existing owner-mediated workflow, accepting that the reported automatic recovery remains unavailable.

recommendation.title: Approve the narrow hook contract
recommendation.body: Keep only `resetSession(reason?)` on successful, unlocked after-compaction contexts with lifecycle-owned draining, documentation, focused compatibility tests, and complete live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses core agent orchestration, session reset behavior, bundled harnesses, and the Codex runtime boundary represented in recent merged work.
